from pysat.solvers import Glucose3
from pysat.card import CardEnc, EncType
import itertools

n = 15
edges = []
edge_vars = {}
var_counter = 1

for i in range(n):
    for j in range(i + 1, n):
        edges.append((i, j))
        edge_vars[(i, j)] = var_counter
        edge_vars[(j, i)] = var_counter
        var_counter += 1

solver = Glucose3()

# Degree constraints
for i in range(n):
    incident_vars = [edge_vars[(i, j)] for j in range(n) if i != j]
    # degree >= 3
    cnf_ge = CardEnc.atleast(lits=incident_vars, bound=3, encoding=EncType.seqcounter, top_id=var_counter)
    for clause in cnf_ge.clauses:
        solver.add_clause(clause)
    var_counter = max([abs(l) for clause in cnf_ge.clauses for l in clause] + [var_counter]) + 1
    
    # degree <= 6
    cnf_le = CardEnc.atmost(lits=incident_vars, bound=6, encoding=EncType.seqcounter, top_id=var_counter)
    for clause in cnf_le.clauses:
        solver.add_clause(clause)
    var_counter = max([abs(l) for clause in cnf_le.clauses for l in clause] + [var_counter]) + 1

# No cycles of length 3
for c in itertools.combinations(range(n), 3):
    solver.add_clause([-edge_vars[(c[0], c[1])], -edge_vars[(c[1], c[2])], -edge_vars[(c[0], c[2])]])

# No cycles of length 4
for c in itertools.combinations(range(n), 4):
    for p in itertools.permutations(c):
        # To avoid duplicates, only consider permutations where p[0] is min, and p[1] < p[3]
        if p[0] == min(p) and p[1] < p[3]:
            solver.add_clause([-edge_vars[(p[0], p[1])], -edge_vars[(p[1], p[2])], -edge_vars[(p[2], p[3])], -edge_vars[(p[3], p[0])]])

# No cycles of length 5
for c in itertools.combinations(range(n), 5):
    for p in itertools.permutations(c):
        if p[0] == min(p) and p[1] < p[4]:
            solver.add_clause([-edge_vars[(p[0], p[1])], -edge_vars[(p[1], p[2])], -edge_vars[(p[2], p[3])], -edge_vars[(p[3], p[4])], -edge_vars[(p[4], p[0])]])

print("Solving...")
result = solver.solve()
print("Satisfiable:", result)
if result:
    model = solver.get_model()
    solution = [e for e in edges if model[edge_vars[e] - 1] > 0]
    print("Solution:", solution)

        solver.add_clause(clause)
    var_counter = max([abs(l) for clause in cnf_le.clauses for l in clause] + [var_counter]) + 1

# No cycles of length 3
for c in itertools.combinations(range(n), 3):
    solver.add_clause([-edge_vars[(c[0], c[1])], -edge_vars[(c[1], c[2])], -edge_vars[(c[0], c[2])]])

# No cycles of length 4
for c in itertools.combinations(range(n), 4):
    for p in itertools.permutations(c):
        if p[0] == min(p) and p[1] < p[3]:
            solver.add_clause([-edge_vars[(p[0], p[1])], -edge_vars[(p[1], p[2])], -edge_vars[(p[2], p[3])], -edge_vars[(p[3], p[0])]])

# No cycles of length 5
for c in itertools.combinations(range(n), 5):
    for p in itertools.permutations(c):
        if p[0] == min(p) and p[1] < p[4]:
            solver.add_clause([-edge_vars[(p[0], p[1])], -edge_vars[(p[1], p[2])], -edge_vars[(p[2], p[3])], -edge_vars[(p[3], p[4])], -edge_vars[(p[4], p[0])]])

print("Solving...")
result = solver.solve()
print("Satisfiable:", result)
if result:
    model = solver.get_model()
    solution = [e for e in edges if model[edge_vars[e] - 1] > 0]
    print("Solution:", solution)
